156:     sm = np.zeros((len(P), len(Q)))  # The score matrix
157:     for iP, occ_P in enumerate(P):
158:         for iQ, occ_Q in enumerate(Q):
159:             if similarity_metric == "cardinality_score":
160:                 denom = float(np.max([len(occ_P), len(occ_Q)]))
161:                 # Compute the score
162:                 sm[iP, iQ] = len(_occurrence_intersection(occ_P, occ_Q)) / denom
163:             # TODO: More scores: 'normalised matching socre'
164:             else:
165:                 raise ValueError(
166:                     "The similarity metric (%s) can only be: " "'cardinality_score'."
167:                 )
168:     return sm
169: 
170: 
171: def standard_FPR(reference_patterns, estimated_patterns, tol=1e-5):
172:     """Compute the standard F1 Score, Precision and Recall.
173: 
174:     This metric checks if the prototype patterns of the reference match
175:     possible translated patterns in the prototype patterns of the estimations.
176:     Since the sizes of these prototypes must be equal, this metric is quite
177:     restrictive and it tends to be 0 in most of 2013 MIREX results.
178: 
179:     Examples
180:     --------
181:     >>> ref_patterns = mir_eval.io.load_patterns("ref_pattern.txt")
182:     >>> est_patterns = mir_eval.io.load_patterns("est_pattern.txt")
183:     >>> F, P, R = mir_eval.pattern.standard_FPR(ref_patterns, est_patterns)
184: 
185:     Parameters
186:     ----------
187:     reference_patterns : list
188:         The reference patterns using the format returned by
189:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_patterns()`
190:     estimated_patterns : list
191:         The estimated patterns in the same format
192:     tol : float
193:         Tolerance level when comparing reference against estimation.
194:         Default parameter is the one found in the original matlab code by
195:         Tom Collins used for MIREX 2013.
196:         (Default value = 1e-5)
197: 
198:     Returns
199:     -------
200:     f_measure : float
201:         The standard F1 Score
202:     precision : float
203:         The standard Precision
204:     recall : float
205:         The standard Recall
206: 
207:     """
208:     validate(reference_patterns, estimated_patterns)
209:     nP = len(reference_patterns)  # Number of patterns in the reference
210:     nQ = len(estimated_patterns)  # Number of patterns in the estimation
211:     k = 0  # Number of patterns that match
212: 
213:     # If no patterns were provided, metric is zero
214:     if _n_onset_midi(reference_patterns) == 0 or _n_onset_midi(estimated_patterns) == 0:
215:         return 0.0, 0.0, 0.0
216: 
217:     # Find matches of the prototype patterns
218:     for ref_pattern in reference_patterns:
219:         P = np.asarray(ref_pattern[0])  # Get reference prototype
220:         for est_pattern in estimated_patterns:
221:             Q = np.asarray(est_pattern[0])  # Get estimation prototype
222: 
223:             if len(P) != len(Q):
224:                 continue
225: 
226:             # Check transposition given a certain tolerance
227:             if len(P) == len(Q) == 1 or np.max(np.abs(np.diff(P - Q, axis=0))) < tol:
228:                 k += 1
229:                 break
230: 
231:     # Compute the standard measures
232:     precision = k / float(nQ)
233:     recall = k / float(nP)
234:     f_measure = util.f_measure(precision, recall)
235:     return f_measure, precision, recall
236: 
237: 
238: def establishment_FPR(
239:     reference_patterns, estimated_patterns, similarity_metric="cardinality_score"
240: ):
241:     """Compute the establishment F1 Score, Precision and Recall.
242: 
243:     Examples
244:     --------
245:     >>> ref_patterns = mir_eval.io.load_patterns("ref_pattern.txt")
246:     >>> est_patterns = mir_eval.io.load_patterns("est_pattern.txt")
247:     >>> F, P, R = mir_eval.pattern.establishment_FPR(ref_patterns,
248:     ...                                              est_patterns)
249: 
250:     Parameters
251:     ----------
252:     reference_patterns : list
253:         The reference patterns in the format returned by
254:         :func:`mir_eval.io.load_patterns()`
255: 
256:     estimated_patterns : list
257:         The estimated patterns in the same format
258: 
259:     similarity_metric : str
260:         A string representing the metric to be used when computing the
261:         similarity matrix. Accepted values:
262: 
263:             - "cardinality_score": Count of the intersection
264:               between occurrences.
265: 
266:         (Default value = "cardinality_score")
267: 
268:     Returns
269:     -------
270:     f_measure : float
271:         The establishment F1 Score
272:     precision : float
273:         The establishment Precision
274:     recall : float
275:         The establishment Recall
276: 
277:     """
278:     validate(reference_patterns, estimated_patterns)
279:     nP = len(reference_patterns)  # Number of elements in reference
280:     nQ = len(estimated_patterns)  # Number of elements in estimation
281:     S = np.zeros((nP, nQ))  # Establishment matrix
282: 
283:     # If no patterns were provided, metric is zero
284:     if _n_onset_midi(reference_patterns) == 0 or _n_onset_midi(estimated_patterns) == 0:
285:         return 0.0, 0.0, 0.0
286: 
287:     for iP, ref_pattern in enumerate(reference_patterns):
288:         for iQ, est_pattern in enumerate(estimated_patterns):
289:             s = _compute_score_matrix(ref_pattern, est_pattern, similarity_metric)
290:             S[iP, iQ] = np.max(s)
291: 
292:     # Compute scores
293:     precision = np.mean(np.max(S, axis=0))
294:     recall = np.mean(np.max(S, axis=1))
295:     f_measure = util.f_measure(precision, recall)
296:     return f_measure, precision, recall
297: 
298: 
299: def occurrence_FPR(
300:     reference_patterns,
301:     estimated_patterns,
302:     thres=0.75,
303:     similarity_metric="cardinality_score",
304: ):
305:     """Compute the occurrence F1 Score, Precision and Recall.
306: 
307:     Examples
308:     --------
309:     >>> ref_patterns = mir_eval.io.load_patterns("ref_pattern.txt")
310:     >>> est_patterns = mir_eval.io.load_patterns("est_pattern.txt")
311:     >>> F, P, R = mir_eval.pattern.occurrence_FPR(ref_patterns,
